answer: Harbor clerks once let one skipper register a stack of skiff names and collect trap-share on every alias. A skipper may now hold only one marked coral head on a charted reef, tie the workboat to a numbered tide terrace at the 1.4-meter mark, and fire five acoustic echo pings, 21 minutes apart, whose round-trip times must stay within 28 milliseconds of that head's published sounding. Bond is 9.6 coin held for 38 hours. Surveyors replay the ping tapes; if two skiff names share one coral head, one terrace bolt, or one echo envelope, both bonds burn and that head stays dark for twelve epochs.
